title: consistent error schema, retry-after semantics, and idempotency handling for streaming / openai-compat
author: Maya Patel
description: Background: Multiple customer bug reports and internal integration tests showed inconsistent behaviors in the OpenAI compatibility layer and streaming endpoints when rate limits, idempotency conflicts, or internal errors occur. Symptoms included: (1) missing or ambiguous Retry-After semantics across hosted vs dedicated; (2) idempotency keys that sometimes returned a 500 on duplicate requests instead of a deterministic 200/409; (3) streaming clients receiving partial SSE/HTTP chunks with no canonical error envelope; (4) OpenAI-compat mappings returning different error shapes from the main API which caused SDKs to mis-handle retries. Motivation: unify error surface and retry semantics so clients (and our SDKs) can implement robust backoff/retry, and so streaming consumers get a machine-readable error payload at the end of a stream. Changes in this PR: - Standardize HTTP rate-limit headers and Retry-After behavior: always return Retry-After in seconds when throttled and include X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset (unix epoch seconds). For sub-second guidance, include X-Retry-After-Ms only for internal fast-paths (e.g., burst throttles). The OpenAI compat layer maps internal throttles to 429 + {"type":"rate_limit","code":"rate_limit_exceeded"}. - Idempotency key lifecycle: persist Idempotency-Key for successful and in-progress requests for a configurable TTL (default 24h). On duplicate non-mutating calls we now return the original response (200), on duplicate conflicting side-effect attempts we return 409 with code "idempotency_conflict" and an explanatory message. Internal transient errors during idempotency write will trigger a 503 with code "idempotency_unavailable" to avoid unsafe retries. - Streaming stability & error envelope: streaming responses (SSE and chunked JSON) will terminate with a final structured error chunk/trailer when an error occurs mid-stream. The final chunk uses a canonical shape: {"error":{"type":"<type>","code":"<code>","message":"<message>","request_id":"<id>"}} so SDKs can detect and act on the error deterministically. OpenAI-compat GET /v1/chat/streams mapping will include this final JSON chunk and then close the connection. - OpenAI compatibility layer mappings: introduced a single map in openai_compat/error_map.go that translates internal codes (e.g., QUOTA_EXCEEDED, THROTTLE, KV_WRITE_FAIL) into OpenAI-like codes and types so downstream SDKs see consistent errors. - Client-facing docs & tests: updated API reference and added end-to-end tests for rate limit headers, idempotency key replays, and streaming error trailers. - Observability: added new metrics (errors.openai_compat_mapped_total, idempotency.key_hits_total) and traces for idempotency lookups to ease debugging. Related: ENG-2013 implements the idempotency storage change; SUP-432 reported the original customer issue. Checklist: - [x] Rate-limit header canonicalization implemented and tested - [x] Idempotency persistence with TTL and conflict semantics - [x] Streaming final-error envelope implemented for SSE and chunked JSON - [x] OpenAI compat error map and test cases - [x] Docs and SDK compatibility notes updated - [x] End-to-end tests added (CI passing) Notes/Tradeoffs: - We keep Retry-After in seconds as the canonical header to match broad client expectations; X-Retry-After-Ms is best-effort and only available on some throttles. - Persisting idempotency keys increases storage/coordination cost; we use a sharded TTL map and a background compaction job to bound cost. - This PR intentionally avoids changing public error codes used by large enterprise customers; instead we map internal codes to the stable OpenAI-like set. Migration: SDKs should start reading the canonical error envelope on streams and respect the Retry-After header (seconds). For idempotency, clients should pass Idempotency-Key for safe retries and handle 409/idempotency_conflict by surfacing the conflict to the caller.
commits: 7 commits: (1) api: add canonical rate limit headers and Retry-After behavior; (2) compat: add openai_compat error mapper; (3) streaming: finalize with structured error trailer for SSE and chunked JSON; (4) idempotency: persist keys with TTL; (5) storage: add sharded idempotency store + compaction job; (6) docs: update API reference and migration notes; (7) tests: add e2e coverage for streaming/error/retry semantics
release_notes: Standardize error shapes and retry semantics across streaming and OpenAI-compat endpoints; idempotency keys persisted with TTL; streaming now emits a final structured error chunk for deterministic client handling.
review_discussion: Rosa: Can you confirm that Retry-After is always in seconds? Maya: Yes; we kept seconds as canonical; X-Retry-After-Ms is optional and only present for burst throttles. Ethan: LGTM pending minor nits in tests. Devon: Please add a tracing span around idempotency lookup. Maya: Added span and metric. CI initially failed on e2e streaming test due to race; fixed by adding a short stabilization wait and asserting final trailer. Approvals: Ethan approved 2026-02-24, Rosa approved 2026-02-25.
